assessment: The observations identify reported practice and preparation gaps, but do not establish their causes. These two combinations are hypotheses; neither establishes the six-session targets or the coordination ceiling.

openings.claim: Cross a standalone conversation prompt with privately chosen optional language scaffolds and reciprocal speaking turns at the first partner exchange. Everyone receives identical paper options; no proficiency declaration or prior attendance is required. Reserve two six-minute turns per participant within the existing session.
openings.delta: Scaffolds alone may leave unequal airtime; allocated turns alone may leave an occasional attendee unable to enter the topic. The hypothesized interaction is that scaffolds make protected speaking opportunities useful while reciprocal turns ensure opportunities to use them.
openings.prediction: The combination increases the fraction reporting ten useful minutes more than either component alone, particularly among attendees unfamiliar with the topic; observed airtime becomes less unequal.
openings.probe: Across six sessions, rotate consenting pairs among scaffold-only, turns-only, combined, and incumbent conditions. Anonymously sample actual speaking durations and ask about usefulness and topic familiarity. Check whether the combined gain exceeds the sum of separate gains; log preparation and observation effort.
assumptions: Existing prompts can support standalone entry and optional scaffolds.
Participants regard some protected speaking time as useful.
Printing and session timing can fit existing resources; workload remains to be measured.

openings.claim: Cross a dated paper next-session preparation strip with a brief partner restatement at the departure handoff. Partners check the stated task and session date against the strip and correct mismatches; fresh standalone current-session instructions remain available on arrival after any absence.
openings.delta: Paper supplies durable offline information; restatement tests interpretation before departure. Their hypothesized interaction catches stale-task carryover while leaving a usable reminder and distributing checks across pairs.
openings.prediction: Combined use reduces earlier-task answers more than paper alone and preserves next-session recall better than restatement alone.
openings.probe: Compare the components and combination using anonymous unprompted exit answers and next-arrival task recall, recording correction counts, clarification requests, and total weekly coordination minutes.
assumptions: Partners can check simple printed instructions accurately.
A short restatement fits the 75-minute session.
No preparation task becomes an attendance requirement.
